title: Exact small values of m(N,3) for arithmetic progressions with every common difference (Green's Problem 37)
abstract: Let m(N,k) be the least size of a finite set of integers containing, for every d=1,...,N, a k-term arithmetic progression of common difference d (Problem 37 in Green's list; k=3 unless stated). I could not find a table of its values in the literature. With CP-SAT in Z I obtain m(N,3)=3,4,5,6,7,8,8,8,9,10,11,11,12,12,12,13,13 for N=1,...,17. For N<=10 this is also supported by DRUP proofs of SAT instances whose reduction to a finite window is proved in the note; for N=11..17 the lower bounds rest on CP-SAT without a certificate. For N<=27 verified witnesses give upper bounds. The finite window [0,2N] is not harmless: for N=15 the true value is 12 but no 12-element set fits in [0,30]. A few values for k=4 are given. Everything is computational, produced by AI agents, without human review or formal verification of the pipeline.
